channel_drafts.audience_note: Administration and customer service staff in small businesses in Italy.
channel_drafts.body:
Teaching exercise: Studio Riva and the assignment are fictional; the EDPB guide is an authentic public source.

This FAQ helps you recognise an access request and organise its handling with the person responsible for privacy. It is a Studio Riva information initiative based on the general guidance in the EDPB guide; it does not announce a new law.

### How do I recognise an access request?

A person may want to know whether the business processes personal data about them, access that data or receive a copy. These are elements of the right of access described by the EDPB guide. If a request has this content, involve your privacy contact to assess it. [EDPB guide: individuals’ rights](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

### What should I do when it arrives?

As a suggested internal arrangement, record the date received, the channel and the content of the request, then promptly pass it to the privacy contact identified by your business. The guide recommends internal procedures and records of requests and responses. The data controller must respond; the data processor assists it. An internal contact coordinates the work without replacing these roles. [EDPB guide: individuals’ rights](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

### How long is there to respond?

The guide sets out a one-month response period. If a request is too complex and more time is needed, the period may be extended by two further months, provided the person is informed within one month of receipt. The extension is not automatic: raise difficulties promptly with the person responsible for privacy for assessment in the particular case. [EDPB guide: individuals’ rights](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

### What needs to be prepared?

The response includes personal data and information about processing, such as its purposes, the categories of data, recipients, and the retention period or criteria used to determine it. These are examples, not a complete list. Your privacy contact should check all the items in the guide’s access section and identify the relevant data; this FAQ is not a complete response template. [EDPB guide: individuals’ rights](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

### Can I simply send the whole file?

Before providing a copy of personal data, check that doing so will not affect other people’s rights and freedoms, for example where one document contains information about several people. Flag such documents to your privacy contact before sharing them. The guide provides for a free copy of the personal data; any additional copies need separate consideration. [EDPB guide: individuals’ rights](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

### When is a specific assessment needed?

Involve the person responsible for privacy if the request is unclear, the work is complex, other people’s data is involved, or a fee or refusal is being considered. The guide allows a reasonable fee or refusal for requests demonstrably manifestly unfounded or excessive; inconvenience alone does not establish this. If a request will not be granted, the reasons and the options of a complaint to the national authority and a judicial remedy must be communicated within one month. These decisions require an individual assessment. [EDPB guide: individuals’ rights](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

General guidance for businesses in Italy. This FAQ does not determine the response to a real request or replace company procedures. Before use, the professional should review the text and the business should identify its privacy contact.

public_source_notes.text: European Data Protection Board (EDPB), Data protection guide for small business, “Respect individuals’ rights”, sections on handling requests and the right of access; extract captured on 14 September 2026. Official guidance, not legislation.

editorial_value.audience_value: Staff can recognise the content of a request and prepare a useful internal handoff.
editorial_value.banality_check: The FAQ goes beyond a general request to be careful: it identifies receipt information, time limits and review decisions. The proposed internal arrangement is explicitly labelled as a proposal.
editorial_value.decision_enabled: It enables staff to start internal handling and recognise which issues need their privacy contact’s assessment.
editorial_value.decision_limit: General guidance for businesses in Italy. This FAQ does not determine the response to a real request or replace company procedures. Before use, the professional should review the text and the business should identify its privacy contact.
editorial_value.distinct_angle: From initial contact to privacy assessment, separating collection and routing from decisions about the response.
editorial_value.practical_use: Record receipt and content, identify the contact, and flag complexity or other people’s data before responding.
editorial_value.publication_judgment: Useful as a short information draft, subject to professional review; this is not authorisation to distribute it.
editorial_value.reason_now: A firm-led information initiative was requested; no legislative development or exceptional deadline was supplied.
editorial_value.repetition_check: No history was selected, so repetition against prior communications cannot be assessed.
editorial_value.source_specific_information: The guide connects internal procedures with a one-month response period, a conditional extension and a check of others’ rights before supplying a copy.
